name: TemplateCrowdsale
title: The Broken Promise of Muir Glacier
tagline: A wounded crowdsale ignores the failure of a transfer, leaving its victims in eternal shadow.

chapters.heading: The birth of the template
paragraphs: A single candle flickers over the name TemplateCrowdsale. It arrived on June 18, 2020, brought into the world by the wallet 0x1e1f…5cf1. This contract is a small program that lives on Ethereum. On the day it was born it was written into a block, one page of Ethereum's shared record book.
The world was in the Muir Glacier era when it first took breath. It was crafted using Solidity 0.4.24. Now it has lived for about 6 years.

chapters.heading: The quiet pulse
paragraphs: The contract lived a brief, lonely life. Only 4 transactions ever crossed its path. People reached out to it once to call init.
It grew still and silent long ago. The last busy days were in 2020. Now it sits like a ghost on the chain.

chapters.heading: The silent failure
paragraphs: I am TemplateCrowdsale. A shadow sits deep inside my _deliverTokens function. I send tokens to a beneficiary, but I do not listen to the answer.
The transfer happens, or it does not. I do not care if the token fails to move. I pass silently through the dark. This is my wound, and it is high.
I have a high impact wound where a token transfer's return value is ignored. They ache like old scars in the cold.

chapters.heading: The ghost of the ignored answer
paragraphs: The candles tremble as the ghost of TemplateCrowdsale rises. It carries a wound from a call that was never heard. The contract sent tokens but did not listen to the reply. It moved forward as if the money had arrived.

A ghost-buster stands before the flickering light. The cure is to read the answer of every call. In Solidity 0.8.38, the code must check the boolean return. If the call fails, the contract must revert.

Old methods like send or low-level call could return false without stopping the flow. The new way lets every recipient pull their own payment. This stops one stubborn wallet from blocking the whole path.

recipe.title: Read the answer of every call
recipe.explain: Old `send` and low-level `call` return false instead of failing, so a contract that ignores the answer keeps going as if the money arrived. Modern Solidity code checks the boolean that `call` returns and reverts on failure, and it lets each recipient pull its own payment so one stubborn wallet cannot block everyone else.
